newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - BANK OF ENGLAND RAISES UK RATES.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - BANK OF ENGLAND RAISES UK RATES.

text.p: Following is a list of economists reactions to the Bank of England's decision to raise official British interest rates to 7.0 percent.

JEREMY HAWKINS, BANK OF AMERICA: "The Bank of England hike should be seen as at least a small plus for the pound given a very split market going into the result. Impact may nonetheless be limited by speculation that this will be the top of the official rate cycle - at least for now. We see the Monetary Policy Committee leaving rates on hold at the September meeting, but still look for a 7.25 percent base rate before the end of the year as consumer spending continues to gather momentum."

"The important thing about the Bank of England's statement is the clear message from that the current level of rates is consistent with hitting the inflation target. That is a clear signal that the Bank thinks it has done enough for the time being and it believes the move should put downward pressure on sterling. We expect the Bank to say in its inflation report (next week) it will hit the inflation target in two years time. We do not expect another rate rise until November."

"The rate rise was very much as the majority of people had expected. Much more interesting are the bank's comments suggesting that interest rates have reached a level consistent with their target. This will be on the basis that sterling remains at current levels or even appreciates further. If sterling does start to depreciate, which is possible, then clearly further interest rate increases will be needed."

"I think it's true that the Bank is not too worried about the level of sterling right now. They're worried about activity elsewhere and they're sending a firm signal that they're unhappy with the levels of activity because of the inflation risks inherent in that."
